latest_release.body:
These are the release notes for the v1.57.0 release of [Backstage](https://backstage.io/).

A huge thanks to the whole team of maintainers and contributors as well as the amazing Backstage Community for the hard work in getting this release developed and done.

## Highlights

### Front-end system 1.0

The front-end system reaches its 1.0 milestone in this release! The public APIs of `@backstage/frontend-plugin-api`, `@backstage/frontend-app-api`, `@backstage/frontend-test-utils`, and `@backstage/frontend-dev-utils` are now stable under the [package versioning policy](../overview/versioning-policy.md#package-versioning-policy).

The extension-based architecture lets app owners install and configure plugins, customize how features fit together, and share those customizations through frontend modules. This release brings router-independent navigation, lazy Utility API implementations, translated page titles, and a consolidated set of core Utility APIs, alongside the removal of deprecated APIs.

If you are migrating an app, start with the [app migration guide](../frontend-system/building-apps/08-migrating.md). Plugin authors can follow the [plugin migration guide](../frontend-system/building-plugins/05-migrating.md). Apps and plugins already using the front-end system should review the breaking changes below and the [1.57 frontend migration notes](../frontend-system/architecture/60-migrations.md#157).

This milestone focuses on stabilizing the front-end plugin API and its surrounding architecture. Work on documentation, examples, and features continues, and adopters can expect further updates in those areas.

### **BREAKING**: Router-independent frontend navigation

The front-end system now owns the browser history, while each page can choose its own routing library. Three new adapter packages support React Router v6, React Router v7, and TanStack Router, including pages that host sub-pages using a different library. Existing pages retain implicit React Router v6 compatibility. Framework navigation APIs such as `useAppNavigate`, `useAppLocation`, and `RouterLink` let plugins navigate without depending on a page's router. Router and component-library integrations use the stable `@backstage/frontend-plugin-api/routing` entry point, while app history is available through `coreApis.appHistory` in the main entry point.

`RouterBlueprint`, the `app/root` router input, and `convertLegacyAppOptions({ components: { Router } })` are no longer supported. Remove overrides that only install a `BrowserRouter`, move global providers to `AppRootWrapperBlueprint`, and render page adapters inside lazily loaded page components. Framework navigation destinations must start with `/` and exclude the deployment basename; use a page adapter for path-relative navigation. `useRouteRefParams` now returns only the parameters declared by its route ref, without an undeclared splat parameter. Apps using the old front-end system keep their existing routing setup.

Backstage UI routing is configured automatically in Backstage apps. Standalone apps must provide a `useNavigation` hook to `BUIProvider` if they previously relied on automatic React Router integration. `routerOptions` now only accepts `replace` and `state`, and links using `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` become inert. See the [routing migration notes](../frontend-system/architecture/60-migrations.md#157) and [page router guide](../frontend-system/building-plugins/10-page-routers.md) for setup and migration examples.

### **BREAKING**: Deprecated frontend APIs removed

This release removes several deprecated APIs from the front-end system and introduces further deprecations. Update custom extensions and API implementations when upgrading:

- Use `DialogApi.open` with your own dialog presentation instead of `show` or `showModal`, and `IconsApi.icon` instead of `getIcon`. Upgrade `@backstage/plugin-app` alongside `@backstage/frontend-plugin-api`; the API references are now `core.dialog.v2` and `cor

## What is Backstage?

[Backstage](https://backstage.io/) is an open source framework for building developer portals. Powered by a centralized software catalog, Backstage restores order to your microservices and infrastructure and enables your product teams to ship high-quality code quickly without compromising autonomy.

Backstage unifies all your infrastructure tooling, services, and documentation to create a streamlined development environment from end to end.

![software-catalog](docs/assets/header.png)

Out of the box, Backstage includes:

- [Backstage Software Catalog](https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/) for managing all your software such as microservices, libraries, data pipelines, websites, and ML models
- [Backstage Software Templates](https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-templates/) for quickly spinning up new projects and standardizing your tooling with your organization’s best practices
- [Backstage TechDocs](https://backstage.io/docs/features/techdocs/) for making it easy to create, maintain, find, and use technical documentation, using a "docs like code" approach
- Plus, a growing ecosystem of [open source plugins](https://github.com/backstage/backstage/tree/master/plugins) that further expand Backstage’s customizability and functionality

Backstage was created by Spotify but is now hosted by the [Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)](https://www.cncf.io) as an Incubation level project. For more information, see the [announcement](https://backstage.io/blog/2022/03/16/backstage-turns-two#out-of-the-sandbox-and-into-incubation).
